answer:
Roughly half the training data is correct in both Self-Instruct and s1, and both papers keep the wrong examples on purpose. OpenThoughts finds that filtering answers with a GPT verifier makes the trained model slightly worse, not better.

| Paper | What was measured | Share correct |
|---|---|---|
| Self-Instruct | Generated examples with instruction, input and output all valid | **54%** |
| s1 | Distilled answers in s1K judged correct | **53.6%** (63.0% in s1K-1.1) |
| OpenThoughts | Effect of GPT-4o-mini answer verification | No share given; it lowers scores, 40.0 vs 41.6 for random filtering |

**Self-Instruct.** One author labelled 200 generated instructions, one instance each ([p. 4, §3.3](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/data/Self-Instruct.%20Aligning%20Language%20Models%20with%20Self-Generated%20Instructions.pdf?dest=subsection.3.3&page=4)). The results are in [p. 4, Table 2](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/data/Self-Instruct.%20Aligning%20Language%20Models%20with%20Self-Generated%20Instructions.pdf?dest=table.2&page=4):
- the instruction describes a valid task: 92%;
- the input fits the instruction: 79%;
- the output is correct: 58%;
- **all three fields valid: 54%.**

The authors argue that most of the wrong examples are still in the right format or partly correct, so they still help training (p. 4). Better data does help, though: regenerating every output with InstructGPT-003 improves the model by 10% in human evaluation ([p. 8, Figure 7](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/data/Self-Instruct.%20Aligning%20Language%20Models%20with%20Self-Generated%20Instructions.pdf?dest=figure.7&page=8)).

**s1.** The paper keeps incorrect distilled answers on purpose, because it cares about the reasoning process more than about fully correct solutions. Its grader judges **53.6% of s1K correct**, and 63.0% of the follow-up s1K-1.1, whose traces were regenerated with DeepSeek R1 ([p. 3, §2.2](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/data/s1.%20Simple%20test-time%20scaling.pdf?dest=subsection.2.2&page=3); [p. 16, App. A](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/data/s1.%20Simple%20test-time%20scaling.pdf?dest=appendix.A&page=16)). An LLM compares each answer with the reference solution. Claude 3.7 graded the final 1,000 samples; Claude 3.5 did the grading used to select them ([p. 19, §C.3](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/data/s1.%20Simple%20test-time%20scaling.pdf?dest=subsection.C.3&page=19)).

**OpenThoughts.** It reports no share of correct answers. It tests whether removing answers judged wrong improves the trained model:
- **Setup:** 63,200 math answers are generated, each filter is applied, and 31,600 pairs are sampled from what remains. "GPT Verification" asks GPT-4o-mini whether each answer is correct ([p. 9, §4.5](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/data/OpenThoughts.%20Data%20Recipes%20for%20Reasoning%20Models.pdf?dest=subsection.4.5&page=9); prompt on p. 59, §R.4.1).
- **Result:** GPT verification scores **40.0** on average, below random filtering at 41.6 and no filtering at 41.9. Its math average drops to 61.4, against 64.8 and 65.6. Only science is higher: 48.3 against 46.7 and 46.4 ([p. 9, Table 7](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/data/OpenThoughts.%20Data%20Recipes%20for%20Reasoning%20Models.pdf?dest=table.7&page=9)).
- **Conclusion:** no filter beat using all answers, so OpenThoughts3 does no answer filtering at all (p. 9; p. 30).
- **Earlier datasets:** in the older OpenThoughts-114K, verification raised the 32B model's average from 62.1 to 64.5. It lowered the 7B model's from 45.0 to 41.9 ([p. 30, Table 15](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/data/OpenThoughts.%20Data%20Recipes%20for%20Reasoning%20Models.pdf?dest=table.15&page=30)).

**Overall:** about half of each training set was correct, and that was enough. OpenThoughts adds that a correctness filter doesn't pay for the data it throws away, at least for 7B models trained on math. One caveat: Self-Instruct's 54% rests on 200 examples labelled by a single author.

These numbers come from the library's markdown copies (all converted from arXiv HTML) and agree with the papers' notes. I did not check them against the PDFs. Nothing changed, so there is no commit.
